prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web application mockup, landscape 1536×1024
Input image: REFERENCE IMAGE ONLY. Use /tmp/codex-clipboard-npXubF.png solely as incumbent visual-system reference for browser/app chrome, palette, typography, density, and component character. Do not edit it and do not preserve its split-pane layout or existing page content.
Primary request: Design a structure-led Baseball Dashboard dedicated one-game “Player Props” page for Cincinnati Reds at San Francisco Giants. This is an analytical decision surface for a broad range of baseball bettors, not a sportsbook bet slip.
Composition: Full-width single-page desktop app inside the incumbent browser/app frame. At top, retain the slim dark-green Baseball Dashboard app header. Under it, add a breadcrumb “← Back to CIN at SF”, then a compact game identity strip showing CIN at SF, Oracle Park, Mon 6:45 PM PDT, probable pitcher context, and restrained controls such as “All props”, “Batters”, and a compact “Best leans — all games” link/button.
Next section: a compact full-width scoring console titled “LEAN SCORE WEIGHTS” with three horizontal sliders labeled exactly “Model confidence”, “Statistical edge”, and “Market value”. Show current weights clearly as 40%, 35%, 25%, with “Total 100%” and a concise formula explanation that cumulative score updates as weights change. Use short tick marks, numeric values, and clean controls, not playful knobs.
Focal module: Immediately below, create a decisive but sober “TOP LEAN” module highlighting “Jung Hoo Lee — Over 0.5 hits” as the current strongest lean. Give it a large cumulative score such as “82.4” with “out of 100”, but do not make it look guaranteed. Show explicit uncertainty language such as “Moderate uncertainty · alternatives are close”, market odds such as “Over −243 · Under +179”, and all three factor values: “Model confidence 84”, “Statistical edge 79”, “Market value 81”. Include a compact evidence ledger with believable analytical rows such as season hit rate, recent form, opposing pitcher split, projected plate appearances, and price penalty. Use mixed positive/neutral evidence indicators. Beside or beneath the focal card, show two “Close alternatives” rows with scores like 80.9 and 79.7 so the top pick is clearly not absolute.
Below: a dense ranked comparison table titled “ALL PLAYER PROPS” containing all remaining one-game props. Provide compact filters and sort controls: search field, Team: All, Market: All, Direction: All, and “Sort: Cumulative score”. Table columns: rank, player / team, prop, direction, line, odds, model confidence, statistical edge, market value, cumulative score. Include about 8–10 plausible rows such as O. Basabe over 0.5 hits, Rafael Devers over 0.5 hits, Chase Burns under 6.5 strikeouts, Bryce Eldridge over 0.5 hits, Drew Gilbert over 0.5 hits, Buddy Kennedy under 0.5 hits, and others. Make score differences visually scannable with restrained small bars or numeric cells, never loud badges.
Visual style: Carry over the incumbent screenshot’s Baseball Dashboard identity: background #101613, panels #18211c, primary text #e8eae6, gold #e5b54e, coral #e07b6c, powder blue #82aecf. IBM Plex / Barlow condensed scorecard feel, narrow uppercase section headings, flat panels, 1px hairline rules, crisp tabular figures, compact spacing, small gold eyebrow ticks. Preserve the serious baseball-analysis mood. Use coral for over/positive direction and powder blue for under/negative direction sparingly; gold only for hierarchy and selected controls.
Hierarchy: The top lean and its evidence must be the focal point, sliders second, table third. Keep information density high yet legible, with clean alignment and generous enough row height for scanning. Make the page look fully designed and production-ready rather than like a wireframe.
Exact visible labels to prioritize: “BASEBALL DASHBOARD”, “PLAYER PROPS”, “LEAN SCORE WEIGHTS”, “Model confidence”, “Statistical edge”, “Market value”, “Total 100%”, “TOP LEAN”, “Jung Hoo Lee”, “Over 0.5 hits”, “Moderate uncertainty · alternatives are close”, “Close alternatives”, “ALL PLAYER PROPS”, “Cumulative score”, “Best leans — all games”.
Constraints: one desktop page, no sidebar, no split-pane game detail, no decorative hero, no gradients, no glassmorphism, no neon, no glossy effects, no large empty areas, no sportsbook bet-slip chrome, no bet buttons, no guarantees, no fake win-rate claims, no promotional copy, no fake logos, no watermark. Maintain realistic readable UI text and coherent alignment.
